title: Anthropic polled 1,334 of its employees. They're more sure than most of us that AI will take over jobs.
summary:
Anthropic employees believe that AI will make their labor obsolete.
The AI company published research on Friday that compares surveys with US adults against an internal poll of 1,334 Anthropic employees.
Anthropic workers are far more optimistic about the progress of AI capabilities, how much it's already saving time, and how fast the economy will grow.
Anthropic workers expect higher unemployment and extreme GDP growthAnthropic's surveys examined how workers already use AI and how they think it will change.
Anthropic employees have larger budgets for the tools and often get access to unreleased models.

title: Why AI Isn’t Ready to Tackle Our Convoluted Genomes
summary:
But if DNA really does harbor some greater secret about how life works, biologists have yet to find it.
In fact, the human genome is less a script than a puzzle that gets harder the closer they look.
Knowing the entire sequence—the order of all 3 billion or so of our DNA’s chemical building blocks, nearly fully deduced by the international Human Genome Project between 1990 and 2003—hasn’t helped much.
That investigation showed that barely 2 percent of the human genome consists of actual genes, the information-coding sequences of DNA.
It’s now clear that understanding the human genome is no longer a matter of figuring out what each gene does.

title: An Entire Swedish TV Show Got Deleted, and AI Got Blamed
summary:
A TV4 system failure wiped out hundreds of hours of work, and Sweden’s Aftonbladet newspaper reported that an AI agent was at fault, citing unnamed sources at the production company, called Mastiff.
The Swedish series was due to return on Nov. 22, but has been delayed indefinitely, TV4 said in a statement.
The TV4 network denies the Aftonbladet report that an AI agent deleted the episodes.
“We don’t have the exact details of what happened yet, but it’s not true that this was caused by an AI agent.
While TV4 said an AI agent was not to blame, it did not clarify whether another type of AI might have had some role in the deletion.

title: A Former OpenAI Employee Was Arrested for Bugging a Company Conference Room
summary:
Listen to this postOpenAI found something spying on it from inside its own office walls, and it wasn’t an LLM.
On Tuesday, the Department of Justice announced the arrest of a former OpenAI employee accused of planting a recording device in a conference room at the company’s San Francisco headquarters.
The FBI arrested Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old from Saudi Arabia, on Friday, Oct. 9, after a complaint was filed against him.
OpenAI says there’s no evidence he obtained sensitive information, but the device was sophisticated, and he may have planned to hide more.
Prosecutors say a chatbot account linked to his wife asked how to build and hide an audio recorder, and the family had booked one-way tickets to Saudi Arabia, The New York Times reports.

title: Calling up Starlink customer service? You'll be talking to Grok.
summary:
Elon Musk's AI is a talker.
This week, Musk's combined AI-and-space-exploration company, SpaceX, announced a new Grok Voice model — and revealed that Starlink call centers are already using the AI-as-a-conversationalist technology to answer 20,000 customer calls a day.
Grok Voice agents are verifying customers, troubleshooting Starlink hardware, issuing credits, and shipping replacement equipment, the company said.
That makes Starlink a useful, real-world test case for AI voice technology — and particularly useful for its global expansion.
The company says Starlink serves more than 6 million active customers around the world.

title: Meta’s new terms may allow it to train AI on news sites for free
summary:
The new terms, which go into effect on October 30th, say Meta can use this outside content to “develop, improve, research,” and “train” its AI products.
While Meta spokesperson Daniel Roberts says that the company is just “consolidating” its commercial and self-serve ad terms, legal experts tell Nieman Lab that this could allow Meta “to argue its commercial terms supersede other blocking instructions,” like a site’s robots.txt file.
That could potentially allow Meta to bypass a licensing agreement and freely train its AI models on content posted by online publishers.
Meta may use any content from such domains, web pages, or URLs to provide, develop, improve, research, train, and maintain the integrity of, the Meta Company Products, services, and features provided under these Commercial Terms and any other applicable supplemental terms.
Andy Stone, Meta’s vice president of communications, writes in a post on X that this change isn’t meant to target news sites.

title: IBM talent exec says it's better to be a specialist, not a generalist, in the AI era
summary:
It's a hotly debated question: Is it better to be an expert or a generalist in the AI era?
For Aparna Nair, IBM's chief talent, leadership, and culture officer, there's no debate.
She said she doesn't think generalists alone "will cut it" in the workforce in the AI era.
IBM is hired for its deep technological expertise, she said.
Nair said that there's "nothing more powerful" than when workers combine deep expertise with the right behaviors, and also use AI to their advantage.
